games.name: Banjo-Kazooie
games.summary: Banjo-Kazooie as a native Linux game: HarbourMasters' Lighthouse, built from your own cartridge dump.
games.description:
Lighthouse is HarbourMasters' PC port of Banjo-Kazooie, built on the game's decompilation. It runs natively (no emulator, no Proton) at any resolution and frame rate, with widescreen, mods and romhacks, and an in-game menu for graphics, controls and enhancements.

The game's data comes from your own Banjo-Kazooie cartridge dump (USA 1.0 or 1.1, Japan or Europe; USA 1.0 if you want romhacks): piShop checks it and puts it in the game's folder, and at the first start Lighthouse builds its assets from it (bk.o2r). Settings, saves and mods stay in the game's folder.
steamos: First start: Lighthouse offers to build the game's assets. Answer Yes, Yes again to process the ROM it found, then Yes to run the game. The controller works in these prompts, and it only happens once.

parts.name: Banjo-Kazooie ROM
parts.description: Your own cartridge dump: USA 1.0 or 1.1, Japan or Europe, in .z64 byte order.

install.source:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Banjo-Kazooie through Lighthouse (HarbourMasters), the Linux AppImage.
#
# piShop has already extracted the Lighthouse Linux zip into this game's
# folder (the current folder, $PISHOP_GAME_DIR): lighthouse.appimage,
# gamecontrollerdb.txt and readme.txt. The ROM ($PISHOP_PART_ROM) was checked
# against the supported dumps' SHA-1.
#
# Lighthouse keeps its settings, saves, mods and bk.o2r (built from the ROM
# at the first start) in $SHIP_HOME, and looks for the ROM there. The
# launcher below points SHIP_HOME at this folder, so everything stays
# together when piShop moves the game.
#
# Safe to run again.
set -euo pipefail

echo "::step Checking Lighthouse"
app=$(find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -iname '*.appimage' -print -quit)
if [[ -z $app ]]; then
  echo "No AppImage in the Lighthouse download." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ $app != ./lighthouse.appimage ]]; then
  mv -f "$app" lighthouse.appimage
fi
chmod +x lighthouse.appimage

echo "::step Adding your ROM"
cp -f "$PISHOP_PART_ROM" baserom.us.z64
chmod 0644 baserom.us.z64

echo "::step Writing the launcher"
cat > lighthouse.sh <<'LAUNCHER'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs Lighthouse from this folder, keeping its data here.
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" || exit 1
export SHIP_HOME="$PWD"
exec ./lighthouse.appimage "$@"
LAUNCHER
chmod +x lighthouse.sh
echo "::progress 100 Ready to play"

games.name: Forza Horizon 2
games.summary: The Xbox One edition of Forza Horizon 2 on SteamOS, through the Azimuth launcher.
games.description:
Azimuth is a wrapper that runs the Xbox One version of Forza Horizon 2 on Windows (and on SteamOS through Proton). It translates the Xbox WinRT calls to Win32 and Xbox DirectX 11.X to desktop DirectX 12. The supported version of the game is 1.0.0.64.

Azimuth is lightweight and reaches 720p60 or 1080p30 on a Steam Deck, so hardware on par or faster with 16 GB of RAM should be good to go.

Main features:
• Resolutions from 720p up to whatever your display uses
• 30 or 60 fps
• Three graphics modes: Low (lower than Xbox One, close to the game's split-screen profile), Default (Xbox One level) and High (shadows and reflections twice as detailed, shadows drawn three times as far, car models from photo mode, 16× anisotropic filtering)
• Anti-aliasing: off, MSAA ×2 or MSAA ×4

piShop points Azimuth at the game's files for you, so the launcher doesn't ask for the folder at the first start. Its settings live in azimuth.ini, in the game's folder.

Includes Extra Options by RokkuDayo: intro skip, change car anywhere, Autodrive (D-Pad Down; any driving input takes control back), all DLC packs and VIP unlocked, independent text and audio languages, 4K liveries, unrestricted photo mode and custom gamerpics. Toggle each one in data/bin/FH2_ExtraOptions.ini (read at game start).
steamos: Controller ignored at “Press A”: on Linux/Proton, Azimuth 0.9.7 only reads the first controller slot. An always-connected generic USB receiver (DragonRise) takes it and your controller is ignored. Turn on “Ignore a generic USB receiver” in Games → Patches.
Runs at 60 fps on a ROG Ally; if it stutters or slows down, pick 30 fps in Azimuth's launcher (frame_rate=30 in data/azimuth.ini).
Extra Options: Autodrive is D-Pad Down. The treasure map unlock is off by default: set UnlockTreasureMap=1 in data/bin/FH2_ExtraOptions.ini.

parts.name: Forza Horizon 2
parts.description: The Xbox One game files, version 1.0.0.64.

parts.name: Extra Options
parts.description: RokkuDayo's quality-of-life mod (0.2.34): its Azimuth files go into data/bin.

install.source:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Forza Horizon 2 (Xbox One, 1.0.0.64) through the Azimuth launcher.
#
# piShop has already extracted, into this game's folder (the current folder,
# $PISHOP_GAME_DIR):
#   ./azimuth.exe, ./data/   ← Azimuth (azimuth-windows.zip)
#   ./Game/                  ← the game's RAR
#   ./Mods/ExtraOptions/     ← RokkuDayo's Extra Options mod
#
# This finds the game's package folder (the one holding Mount/AppxManifest.xml)
# and points Azimuth at it in data/azimuth.ini — where Azimuth keeps its
# settings — so the launcher doesn't ask for the folder at the first start.
# The path is relative to azimuth.exe, as Azimuth itself writes it, so the
# game keeps working when piShop moves the whole folder to another library.
#
# Safe to run again (an update runs it again too): a data/azimuth.ini already
# there is the player's, and only its game_folder line changes.
set -euo pipefail

echo "::step Checking Azimuth"
if [[ ! -f azimuth.exe || ! -d data/bin ]]; then
  echo "Azimuth isn't complete in $PWD (azimuth.exe and data/bin are needed)." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "::step Adding Extra Options"
# Its Azimuth build goes into data/bin, replacing Azimuth's azimuth-tls.dll.
mod=Mods/ExtraOptions/Azimuth
if [[ ! -f $mod/azimuth-tls.dll ]]; then
  echo "Extra Options isn't complete in $PWD/$mod." >&2
  exit 1
fi
for f in "$mod"/*; do
  name=${f##*/}
  # The player's own settings stay when this runs again.
  if [[ $name == *.ini && -f data/bin/$name ]]; then
    echo "Keeping data/bin/$name"
    continue
  fi
  cp -f "$f" "data/bin/$name"
  echo "data/bin/$name"
done

echo "::step Finding the game's files"
manifest=$(find Game -maxdepth 4 -type f -path '*/Mount/AppxManifest.xml' -print -quit)
if [[ -z "$manifest" ]]; then
  echo "No Mount/AppxManifest.xml under Game/: the archive isn't Forza Horizon 2's package." >&2
  exit 1
fi
package=$(dirname "$(dirname "$manifest")")
echo "Game package: $package"
for need in era.vbi EmbeddedXvd; do
  if [[ ! -e "$package/$need" ]]; then
    echo "Warning: $package/$need is missing; Azimuth may say the game is incomplete." >&2
  fi
done

echo "::step Pointing Azimuth at the game"
# Windows separators, relative to azimuth.exe: Game\Anthem_1.0.0.64_x64__…
folder=${package//\//\\}
# Azimuth is a Windows program: data/azimuth.ini is UTF-16 with a byte-order
# mark and Windows line ends. Edited as UTF-8 in /tmp, written back the same way.
ini=data/azimuth.ini
edit=/tmp/azimuth.ini
if [[ -f $ini ]]; then
  iconv -f UTF-16 -t UTF-8 "$ini" | tr -d '\r' > "$edit.old"
  found=0
  while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do
    if [[ $line == game_folder=* ]]; then
      printf 'game_folder=%s\n' "$folder"
      found=1
    else
      printf '%s\n' "$line"
    fi
  done < "$edit.old" > "$edit"
  if (( ! found )); then
    printf '[launcher]\ngame_folder=%s\n' "$folder" >> "$edit"
  fi
else
  # Azimuth's own template (0.9.7) with its defaults, but 60 fps (fine on a
  # ROG Ally and a Steam Deck OLED); only game_folder is set.
  cat > "$edit" <<INI
# Azimuth's settings, as key=value lines, which the launcher writes as the
# player changes them. Lines that start with # are not read.
[launcher]
# The game's folder, the one holding Mount: a full path, or one relative to
# the folder of azimuth.exe. The launcher asks for it at the first start and
# saves the folder picked.
game_folder=$folder
# Lines rendered (720, 1080, 1440, 2160, ...), or screen.
resolution=1080
# off, msaax2 or msaax4 (the console's).
antialiasing=msaax4
# low (a steadier frame rate, less power), default (the console's) or
# high (the game engine's higher settings where it has them).
graphics=default
# The channels the game is told the sound output has: system (its own:
# stereo, 5.1 or 7.1), stereo, or multichannel (5.1 or 7.1, which the
# system mixes down for an output with fewer).
audio=system
# 30 or 60.
frame_rate=60
# fixed (the console's): each frame advances the game a fixed step, so it
# slows down while frames run late; real-time: each frame advances the time
# it took, so the game keeps its speed and late frames stutter.
frame_pacing=fixed
# on: frames wait for the display's refresh; off: they show at once, with
# tearing, still paced to the frame rate.
vsync=on
# windowed or fullscreen.
display=fullscreen
# A locale name (en-US, de-DE, pl-PL, ...), or empty for the system's.
language=
# The player's name in the game: 1 to 15 letters, digits and single spaces,
# starting with a letter.
player_name=Player 1
INI
fi
{ printf '\xff\xfe'; awk '{ printf "%s\r\n", $0 }' "$edit" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-16LE; } > "$ini.new"
mv -f "$ini.new" "$ini"
# Earlier revisions of this recipe wrote the settings beside azimuth.exe,
# where Azimuth doesn't look.
rm -f azimuth.ini
echo "game_folder=$folder"
echo "::progress 100 Ready to play"

patches.title: Ignore a generic USB receiver
patches.about: Azimuth only reads the first controller slot. An always-connected generic receiver (DragonRise, USB 0079:0006) takes it, and your controller is ignored at “Press A”. Sets SDL_GAMECONTROLLER_IGNORE_DEVICES=0x0079/0x0006.

games.name: Star Fox 64
games.summary: Star Fox 64 as a native Linux game: HarbourMasters' Starship, built from your own cartridge dump.
games.description:
Starship is HarbourMasters' PC port of Star Fox 64, built on the game's decompilation. It runs natively (no emulator, no Proton) at any resolution and frame rate, with widescreen, mods and an in-game menu for graphics, controls and enhancements.

The game's data comes from your own Star Fox 64 (USA, 1.0 or 1.1) cartridge dump: piShop checks it and puts it in the game's folder as baserom.us.z64; at the first start Starship builds its assets from it (sf64.o2r). The Japanese and European dumps only add voice packs, from the in-game menu later. Settings, saves and mods stay in the game's folder.
steamos: First start: Starship asks for a Star Fox 64 ROM. Answer Yes, pick baserom.us.z64 in the game's folder (the file picker opens there; the touchscreen works), then answer No to “Extract another?”. It only happens once.
Starship 2.0.0 opens in a window: turn on fullscreen in its menu (Esc opens it), or set Window → Fullscreen → Enabled to true in starship.cfg.json.

install.source:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Star Fox 64 through Starship (HarbourMasters), the Linux AppImage.
#
# piShop has already extracted the Starship Linux zip into this game's folder
# (the current folder, $PISHOP_GAME_DIR): starship.appimage, config.yml and
# assets/ (what it extracts the ROM with), mods/, readme.txt and
# gamecontrollerdb.txt. The ROM ($PISHOP_PART_ROM) was checked against the
# USA 1.0/1.1 dumps' SHA-1.
#
# Starship 2.0.0 reads config.yml and assets/ from its working folder and
# writes sf64.o2r there; the game reads it from $SHIP_HOME. The launcher below
# runs it from this folder with SHIP_HOME pointing here, so both agree and
# everything stays together when piShop moves the game.
#
# Safe to run again.
set -euo pipefail

echo "::step Checking Starship"
app=$(find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -iname '*.appimage' -print -quit)
if [[ -z $app ]]; then
  echo "No AppImage in the Starship download." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ $app != ./starship.appimage ]]; then
  mv -f "$app" starship.appimage
fi
chmod +x starship.appimage
if [[ ! -f config.yml || ! -d assets ]]; then
  echo "config.yml or assets/ is missing: Starship can't build its assets without them." >&2
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p mods

# The 2.0.0 zip's gamecontrollerdb.txt is a web page, not the mappings file:
# without it SDL's built-in mappings are used.
if [[ -f gamecontrollerdb.txt ]] && grep -qi '<html' gamecontrollerdb.txt; then
  echo "Removing the broken gamecontrollerdb.txt"
  rm -f gamecontrollerdb.txt
fi

echo "::step Adding your ROM"
cp -f "$PISHOP_PART_ROM" baserom.us.z64
chmod 0644 baserom.us.z64

echo "::step Writing the launcher"
cat > starship.sh <<'LAUNCHER'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs Starship from this folder, keeping its data here.
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" || exit 1
export SHIP_HOME="$PWD"
exec ./starship.appimage "$@"
LAUNCHER
chmod +x starship.sh
echo "::progress 100 Ready to play"

games.name: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
games.summary: Ocarina of Time as a native Linux game: HarbourMasters' Ship of Harkinian, built from your own copy of the game.
games.description:
Ship of Harkinian is HarbourMasters' PC port of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, built on the game's decompilation. It runs natively (no emulator, no Proton) at any resolution and frame rate, with widescreen, the randomizer, mods, and an in-game menu full of enhancements and accessibility options.

The game's data comes from your own copy: any N64 version (USA, Japan or Europe, 1.0 to 1.2), a GameCube release, or Master Quest. piShop checks it and puts it in the game's folder; at the first start Ship of Harkinian builds its assets from it (oot.o2r, or oot-mq.o2r for Master Quest). Settings, saves and mods stay in the game's folder.
steamos: First start: Ship of Harkinian builds the game's assets from your ROM by itself, then asks whether to run the game: answer Yes. It only happens once.
Master Quest too: a second ROM (oot-mq.o2r) can be added later from the in-game menu.

parts.name: Ocarina of Time ROM
parts.description: Your own copy: an N64 version (USA, Japan or Europe), a GameCube release or Master Quest, in .z64 byte order.

source.hint: Your own Ocarina of Time dump (N64, GameCube or Master Quest), in .z64 format

install.source:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time through Ship of Harkinian
# (HarbourMasters), the Linux AppImage.
#
# piShop has downloaded the AppImage ($PISHOP_PART_SOH) and checked the ROM
# ($PISHOP_PART_ROM) against the supported dumps' SHA-1 (N64, GameCube and
# Master Quest versions).
#
# Ship of Harkinian keeps its settings, saves, mods and oot.o2r / oot-mq.o2r
# (built from the ROM) in $SHIP_HOME. The launcher below points SHIP_HOME at
# this folder, so everything stays together when piShop moves the game, and
# until an archive exists it hands the ROM over on the command line: Ship of
# Harkinian then builds it right away, without its file picker.
#
# Safe to run again.
set -euo pipefail

echo "::step Adding Ship of Harkinian"
cp -f "$PISHOP_PART_SOH" soh.appimage
chmod +x soh.appimage

echo "::step Adding your ROM"
cp -f "$PISHOP_PART_ROM" baserom.z64
chmod 0644 baserom.z64

echo "::step Writing the launcher"
cat > soh.sh <<'LAUNCHER'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs Ship of Harkinian from this folder, keeping its data here. The first
# time (no oot.o2r / oot-mq.o2r yet) it gets the ROM to build them from.
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" || exit 1
export SHIP_HOME="$PWD"
if [[ ! -e oot.o2r && ! -e oot-mq.o2r && -f baserom.z64 ]]; then
  exec ./soh.appimage "$PWD/baserom.z64"
fi
exec ./soh.appimage "$@"
LAUNCHER
chmod +x soh.sh
echo "::progress 100 Ready to play"
